findings.issue: The verb advertises a manifest positional (usage block `default-skills (--skills a,b [--replace] | --remove) [manifest]`; verbs-in-full.md `[<manifestPath>]`) but never calls `_manifest_from_positional(args)` as `cmd_reindex` (and the other id-less verbs) does. The path lands in `args.title` and is silently ignored, so the plan written is the one resolved from --project-dir / CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR / cwd, not the one named. Checked by running both verbs against a scratch repo with a nonexistent manifest path: `reindex /nonexistent/zzz.json` exits 2 with 'manifest not found: /nonexistent/zzz.json', while `default-skills --remove /nonexistent/zzz.json` ignores the path and answers about the scratch repo's own plan. A caller who names plan X and gets plan Y written is the lock/journal/manifest split the helper's own docstring warns of. No case passes a manifest positional, so dsv1/dsv2 cannot see it.
findings.resolution: Call `_manifest_from_positional(args)` first in cmd_default_skills, before `_resolve_project`, and add a dsv case that passes the plan path as the positional with a different --project-dir and asserts the named plan changed and a nonexistent path is refused by name.

intent.note: Clause 'Add a plan-wide default ... a new meta key read first by resolve_skills, before area defaults and the task's own ... document it there and in the schema ... with task.skills null still opting out': done. _areas had no existing mechanism, so meta.defaultSkills is correct; resolve_skills builds levels plan default, area tags, task, dedupes at first mention, and the null opt-out returns [] before any level is read (ds3). COMPATIBILITY.md holds the promise: the key is optional, absent or [] resolves byte for byte as before (ds6), KNOWN_META and the schema carry it, and the only change for a plan that writes it is which skills a no-area phase resolves; an older plugin reading such a plan warns on an unknown key at worst. Clause 'Declare this repository's Python house skills there through the plugin's own verb': NOT done (executor's outcome: 'post-merge step'), so the description and the executor's narrowed claim differ - finding 2. Clause 'the validator accepts the key and rejects a non-list': done (validate_default_skills via _check_areas, ds8-ds11, dsk1-dsk3; null is refused as a non-list). The outcome otherwise describes the diff accurately (its casesAdded lists only ds1-ds3 against the eleven ds cases, harmless). Weighed points: (1) COMPATIBILITY kept - adding is free, nothing existing changes meaning. (2) default-skills refusals mirror build-command's (existing without --replace, --replace on none, --remove on none, --remove beside the value flags, free-text/machine check, journal+validator through _under_lock/_write_plan) except the manifest positional it advertises and ignores - finding 1. (3) Plan default is visible wherever resolution is shown because every surface calls resolve_skills: the executor brief (audit-lookup.py:652), doctor, the status portability block, the report, the schema help topic and drive-phase's session start (drive-phase.py:1787, so P138.1's session record names them). The panel does not show it (it shows a task's own skills and an area's, never a resolved list, as before); not a gap against this phase's outcome, though three prose statements still describe the old two-level order - finding 3.
